title: analytics: the native dataset face answers 200 with wrong counts for = / $in / $ne on a single-value image or file field (stored as JSON) where the data door refuses 400
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by the seat's contract review of PR #36184 (#36168), record on that PR; outside #36168's `multiple` population.

## What happens
The data door refuses the JSON-incompatible comparison operators on a second JSON-column class, `single-value-media`: a single-value `image` / `file` field stored as JSON (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts:434-437`). PR #36184's dataset refusal reads only the `multiple` population (`packages/services/service-analytics/src/json-column-comparison-refusal.ts:92-93`, `isJsonStoredShape` in `contains-membership-sql.ts:59-62`), so the native dataset face still answers. Measured on a fresh SQLite deployment, 4 rows, `pic: image`, one row holding `file_1`:

| Filter | Data door | ObjectQL face | Native face | Draft preview |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{pic: 'file_1'}`, `{pic: {$in: ['file_1']}}` | 400 | 400 | 200, count 0 | 200, count 1 |
| `{pic: {$ne: 'file_1'}}` | 400 | 400 | 200, count 4 | 200, count 3 |

Pre-existing on main. The analytics host has no hook today for the column's storage state, which is why #36184 did not take it.

## Done when
The native dataset face (and the draft preview) refuse the same operators, with the same code and sentence, on a single-value media field stored as JSON, through #36184's module; pins on `image` and `file` with a scalar control. Narrows what the door answers ⇒ `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`.

reach: dataset / dashboard filter on an image or file field, measured on SQLite by the reviewer; other dialects to be measured by the claimant.
Business reason: a dashboard filtering on an attachment field shows wrong counts with no error.
Reader: area:reports / domain:server (service-analytics).
Dedupe: `single-value-media dataset` → 0 hits.
Grade: p2 — same class as #36168, rarer field use (filtering by an attachment value).
